claim: Nx 23.1.0 was the latest stable release on 2026-07-17.
The repository's mixed Nx 21/22 starting graph was unsupported and is now aligned on 23.1.0.
The upgrade automatically adopts graph, daemon, cache, TypeScript-config, and startup improvements from Nx 22 and 23.
The repository now uses the latest stable direct dependency graph except for a deliberate TypeScript 6 compatibility hold; Vite is 8.1.5 and TypeScript is pinned to the latest 6.x release, 6.0.3.
The fully refreshed workspace is build-, test-, typecheck-, and Nx-sync-compatible with the repository.
Frontend OpenAPI type drift was generated-artifact ordering debt, not a persistent toolchain incompatibility.
The frontend Vitest target is inferred and no longer carries the explicit executor removed in Nx 24.
Nx Cloud remote caching and task sandboxing merit a controlled pilot, not automatic enablement.
ReleaseGraph and filtered release flows may benefit the multi-package release process.
legacy-peer-deps has been removed; remaining strict peer failures are visible upstream metadata gaps that should be tracked without downgrading the verified latest graph.
The current Vite, TypeScript, React Router, Zod, LangChain, AI SDK, and ESLint releases contain concrete capabilities worth targeted repository pilots.
Remaining audit findings require reachability analysis and upstream/replacement work rather than npm's forced direct-package downgrades.
Docs typechecking now owns and caches its React Router generated-type prerequisite, so it passes from a cold generated state.
CI now rejects Nx synchronization drift before running affected lint, test, and build targets.
Every versioned GitHub Action reference in the repository uses its latest published major release line.
